jobs.title: DEPUTY DIRECTOR II  RESTORATIVE & PREVENTION SERVICES (0952) (PEX)
jobs.description:
Company Description

The San Francisco Adult Probation Department (SFAPD) values the individuality and diversity of justice-involved adults, recognizes the unique challenges they face, and invests in their success through services designed to help them permanently exit the criminal justice system. SFAPD's pretrial, reentry, and rehabilitative services complement its supervision strategies by providing a unique blend of opportunity and accountability. The Department extends a continuum of integrated services to address clients' criminogenic needs and empower them to become productive members of the community. SFAPD dedicates endless energy toward enhancing public safety, seeking victim restoration, enforcing court-ordered accountability, providing structured evidence-based supervision, and operating comprehensive pretrial services on behalf of the Superior Court of San Francisco.

Job Description

Reporting directly to the Chief Probation Officer, the 0952 Deputy Director II of Restorative & Prevention Services is a key executive leadership role responsible for directing, strategic planning, and operational scaling across three vital divisions: Pretrial Services, Reentry Services, and Violence Response Services. The Deputy Director provides vision, administrative direction, and executive oversight to ensure seamless, evidence-based, and client-centered care. By leveraging data, expanding service capacity, and cultivating cross-system partnerships with courts, law enforcement, healthcare providers, and community stakeholders, the Deputy Director advances system reform, reduces recidivism, enhances court appearance rates, and promotes long-term public safety and community restoration.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is an accomplished, visionary, and compassionate criminal justice leader with a proven track record of directing complex, multidisciplinary operations and building high-performing teams. This individual possesses deep expertise in evidence-based pretrial practices, risk assessment methodologies, focused deterrence, violence reduction strategies, and continuity-of-care models (including housing stabilization, workforce development, behavioral health, and substance use interventions).

Key professional attributes and competencies of the ideal candidate include:

Strategic & Equity-Centered Leadership: Demonstrated ability to inspire organizational culture, drive care-first reform, address systemic and implicit bias, and elevate professional development for sworn and non-sworn personnel.
Cross-System Collaboration: Expertise in navigating and aligning complex, siloed government systems, collaborating effectively with judges, prosecutors, defense counsel, law enforcement, CBOs, victim advocates, and community leaders.
Data-Driven & Fiscal Acumen: Highly skilled in performance management, outcome evaluation, technology integration, and multi-million-dollar budget oversight, contract administration, and resource allocation.
Subject Matter Mastery: Comprehensive understanding of court processes, criminal records, legal codes, bail statutes, supervision technologies, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive interventions.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

In accordance with Civil Service Commission Rule 109, representative duties include, but are not limited to, the following:

Executive & Strategic Leadership

Provide strategic direction, vision, and administrative oversight for the Pretrial Services, Reentry Services, and Violence Response Services Divisions.
Formulate, enforce, and evaluate division goals, operational standards, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and departmental policies aligned with executive directives and community safety goals.
Serve as a key advisor to the Chief Probation Officer and represent SFAPD in executive decision-making, interagency committees, community forums, and media/public inquiries.
Drive care-first and equity-centered systemic reforms that reduce unnecessary detention, address disproportionate impact, and foster public trust.

Operational Management & Service Integration

Direct division managers and operational teams, ensuring daily service delivery aligns with evidence-based practices, statutory requirements, and quality control standards.
Coordinate and leverage the Community Assessment Services Center (CASC) to establish robust referral pathways for case management, housing, workforce development, legal aid, behavioral health, and court-ordered release conditions.
Oversee the proper application and integration of supervision technologies, electronic monitoring, criminal records systems, and data collection tools.
Review and modernize training curricula for sworn and non-sworn staff to ensure high-quality delivery of trauma-informed, developmentally appropriate, and culturally responsive services.

Fiscal, Contractual & Data Governance

Oversee the development, implementation, and monitoring of multi-million-dollar divisional budgets, resource allocations, and financial reporting.
Manage public and CBO contracts, ensuring optimal resource utilization, operational efficiency, vendor performance, and strict regulatory compliance.
Lead data management, performance metrics, and research efforts to evaluate program impact, inform policy decisions, enhance transparency, and prepare executive reports.

Stakeholder Engagement & Community Partnerships

Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with the Superior Court, District Attorney, Public Defender, Sheriff's Office, law enforcement, CBOs, faith-based partners, and victim advocates.
Conduct stakeholder outreach to secure, maintain, and expand funding, grant opportunities, and strategic support for violence reduction and reentry initiatives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Possession of a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Criminal Justice, Social Work, Public Administration, Behavioral Sciences, Social Sciences, or a closely related field.
Experience: Three (3) years of extensive management experience leading and directing a complex organization or division providing human, social, or criminal justice services (e.g., pretrial, rehabilitation, social welfare, probation, parole, corrections, law enforcement, or administrative/legal services). All three (3) years must include supervisory experience.
License: Possession of a valid California Class 'C' Driver's License.
Substitution Note: Additional qualifying experience may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis (up to a maximum of 2 years). An advanced degree (Master's or Juris Doctor) in Law, Public Administration, Public Policy, Social Work, or a related field may substitute for one (1) year of the required general experience (supervisory experience remains required).

This position requires the ability to work flexible hours, which may include evening meetings and weekend engagements and work duties as necessary to fulfill departmental and community representation duties.

Desirable Qualifications

Advanced Degree (J.D., M.S.W., M.P.A., M.P.P., or M.S.) in a relevant field.
Demonstrated experience directing multi-divisional operations within a large, complex public or non-profit agency.
Extensive legal background or experience practicing law/providing legal counsel within governmental or criminal justice systems.
Deep knowledge of California legal codes, criminal court procedures, bail statutes, and risk assessment instruments.
Proven expertise in evidence-based practices, including focused deterrence, trauma-informed care, restorative justice, and community-based violence intervention.
Direct experience managing programs serving unhoused populations, individuals with serious mental illness, or substance use disorders.
Track record of leveraging technology systems and modern data tools to streamline operations and enhance performance transparency.
Strong experience in multi-million-dollar budget management and CBO contract oversight.

How to Apply:
Interested and qualified applicants should submit a detailed resume and cover letter describing their relevant executive leadership experience, qualifications, and vision for Restorative & Prevention Services to the San Francisco Adult Probation Department Human Resources Division.

Additional Information

The City offers robust health, retirement, and other benefits. For more information please visit: https://sfdhr.org/benefits-overview. This position is represented by the Municipal Executives Association, which has a Memorandum of Understanding with the City that can be found at MOU.

jobs.title: Executive Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Function Summary

Involves developing, interpreting and implementing financial concepts for financial planning, resource planning (dollars), and control of organizational budget. May analyze and prepare recommendations for financial plans, including annual resource allocations, future requirements, and operating forecasts.

Generic Scope

Spends the majority of time (50% or more) achieving organizational objectives through the coordinated achievements of subordinate staff. Establishes departmental goals and objectives, functions with autonomy. Manages the accountability and stewardship of human, financial, and often physical resources in compliance with departmental and organizational goals and objectives. Ensures subordinate supervisors and professionals adhere to defined internal controls. Manages systems and procedures to protect departmental assets.

Custom Scope

The Executive Director of Finance together with the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), has primary responsibility for all aspects of the department’s finances. The Executive Director of Finance directs the department’s finance unit and provides the depth and breadth of management, strategic planning, and financial reporting/analysis expertise required in an administratively complex department with an annual operating budget of approximately $75 million, consisting of professional fee activities, professional services agreements (PSAs), extramural awards, sponsored projects, gifts and endowments, state funding, and medical education programs.

The Executive Director of Finance is responsible for developing, planning, and implementing sustainable financial and revenue management to support the department’s strategic initiatives and operations. The Executive Director of Finance develops long-range strategies and solutions for current complex issues that often cross functional areas, while providing the guidance and expertise needed to effectively implement needed changes, using resources efficiently and minimizing risk. The individual is responsible for audit management, internal controls, and risk assessment and abatement. The Executive Director of Finance reports to the Chief Administrative Officer and is a senior member of the department’s leadership team in managing financial issues with a strong emphasis on administrative systems and internal controls. The position works collaboratively with the UCSF School of Medicine Dean’s Office, DPH, FPO, UCSF Health and all internal/external vendors interacting with the department.

Department Overview

The Department of Emergency Medicine (DEM) provides emergency medical care to over 177,000 patients annually at the UCSF Medical Center at Parnassus, UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospitals at Mission Bay and Oakland, and Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center. DEM administrative and research staff support the work of 90+ full-time faculty and 50+ attending physicians, a residency program, fellowship programs, and over 300 house staff and students each year. Our vision is to be the leader in compassionate, innovative, and equitable emergency care for all people at all times.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Comprehensive knowledge of finance and budget policies, practices and systems; budgeting and reporting techniques; fund accounting; human resource planning; accounting and bookkeeping.
Ability to effectively communicate verbally and in writing in a timely manner.
Interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively across the organization at all levels; ability to interact with diverse populations.
Client services oriented; good listening, critical thinking, and analytical skills.
Ability to multi-task. Strong work ethic, attention to detail, demonstrated success with consistent and timely follow through.
Demonstrated, exceptional planning, problem solving and decision-making skills; demonstrated ability to effectively persuade and negotiate results in complex situations.
At least 6 years of progressively responsible financial management experience, or equivalent experience, encompassing financial management, strategic planning and organizational development, clinical practice management, and human resources management.
At least 5 years of experience as a lead/supervisor/manager.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge and understanding of internal control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
Familiarity with campus and university systems, federal and staff funding agency requirements, campus internal audit rules and regulations, the campus business and finance bulletin, school and department clinical compensation plan, clinical practice rules and regulations, campus expenditure rules and regulations.
Familiarity with policies and programmatic guidelines for ACGME training programs and associated funding.

Required Education

Advanced degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Preferred Certifications

Professional certification preferred.

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
Scion Executive Search (Scion)
has been retained to conduct an immediate search for a strategic, collaborative, and mission-aligned Chief Development Officer
on behalf of Humane Society Silicon Valley (HSSV), a highly regarded organization dedicated to animal welfare. This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished fundraising executive to lead impact-driven philanthropy efforts in support of a mission dedicated to saving lives, keeping families together, and creating a better future for pets and their people .
This is a full-time, predominantly onsite role based in Milpitas, California.

ABOUT HSSV

For more than 95 years, Humane Society Silicon Valley (HSSV) has been a leader in animal welfare, serving pets and people throughout the Bay Area and beyond. As an independent, privately funded nonprofit organization, HSSV provides adoption and foster programs, veterinary care, behavior and training support, community programs, regional rescue partnerships, and resources that help pets and the people who love them thrive together.

HSSV is nationally recognized for its leadership and impact in animal welfare, with a long history of developing and sharing approaches that improve outcomes for animals and strengthen the human-animal bond. Through its Animal Community Center, Community Pet Clinic, and a dedicated network of donors, volunteers, partners, and supporters, HSSV works to save lives, keep families together, expand access to care, and build a stronger safety net for pets and people.

Mission, Vision & Values

HSSV is driven by a mission to save lives, keep families together, and create a better future for pets and their people, with a vision of a world where animals thrive, people experience the power of the human-animal bond, and families have the resources and support to care for their pets.

HSSV is grounded in the values of Kindness, Courage, and Impact
which are brought to life through a collaborative culture centered on empathy, gratitude, belonging, continuous improvement, and celebrating shared success. HSSV encourages their teams to think boldly, drive meaningful change, take thoughtful risks, and work across teams to create lasting impact for animals, people, and the communities they serve.

POSITION OVERVIEW

Reporting directly to the President & Executive Director, the Chief Development Officer serves as a key member of HSSV’s executive leadership team, providing strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s high-impact fundraising and donor engagement efforts. This leader will guide the development and execution of long-term philanthropic strategies that generate sustainable revenue, deepen donor relationships, and align philanthropic support with HSSV’s strategic priorities. The Chief Development Officer will play a critical role in advancing HSSV’s mission while fostering a strong organization-wide culture of philanthropy.

The Chief Development Officer will personally cultivate and steward a targeted portfolio of high-value donors and prospects while providing strategic leadership for the Philanthropy team. The role will oversee individual and major giving, annual giving, planned giving, endowment, institutional giving and grants, donor stewardship, partnerships, and major and principal gift prospects. As a senior leader and visible ambassador for HSSV, this individual will also build strong relationships throughout the community to advance the organization’s philanthropic goals.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, results-driven, and highly collaborative fundraising leader who can translate organizational priorities into clear, measurable philanthropic goals. They will foster a culture rooted in transparency, accountability, partnership, and continuous learning while embedding philanthropy as a shared responsibility across the organization. This leader will bring proven success managing multi-channel fundraising programs, developing data-informed multi-year strategies, cultivating high-capacity donors, and inspiring teams to achieve ambitious goals in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership

Lead the strategic direction and execution of HSSV’s multi-year philanthropy strategy, aligning fundraising initiatives, organizational leadership, operational execution, strategic partnerships, and innovative funding opportunities with HSSV’s mission and strategic priorities to drive sustainable revenue growth and maximize philanthropic impact.
Build strong cross-functional partnerships across HSSV, leverage organizational expertise and shared insights to strengthen donor experiences, advance fundraising efforts, and achieve collective goals.
Cultivate, develop, and empower a high-performing team to achieve fundraising goals and ensure long-term success within an inclusive, collaborative, and mission-driven culture.
Direct the development and execution of capital campaigns and other special fundraising initiatives as needed, building the strategy, infrastructure, and leadership necessary to secure philanthropic support for HSSV’s highest-priority needs. This includes partnering with the President & Executive Director, Board, and key stakeholders to develop compelling cases for support, engage lead donors, and drive campaigns to successful completion.
Develop and implement a results-driven framework that establishes clear goals, measures impact, and fosters accountability, excellence, and continuous learning.
Maintain a personal portfolio of major and principal gift prospects and donors, with direct responsibility for achieving an annual individual fundraising goal through the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-capacity philanthropists and strategic partners.

Culture of Philanthropy

Develop and oversee a culture of philanthropy that strengthens and grows individual giving, major gifts, annual giving, endowment, planned giving, institutional giving, and grants while building a sustainable pipeline of philanthropic support.
Champion a culture of philanthropy across HSSV by fostering cross-functional collaboration, engaging staff and leadership in fundraising efforts, and embedding philanthropy as a shared organizational responsibility.
Build and steward a robust donor engagement strategy that cultivates lifelong supporters, philanthropic leaders, and community ambassadors who advance HSSV's mission and long-term sustainability.

Program Impact

Drive strategic financial leadership by overseeing budget planning and financial management to maximize fundraising effectiveness and operational efficiency.
Provide strategic oversight of Philanthropy operations to ensure an exceptional donor experience through seamless stewardship, effective talent development, and consistent operational excellence.
Lead the strategic use of data, technology, and analytics to strengthen decision-making, enhance fundraising effectiveness, and drive measurable results.
Model and promote the highest standards of ethical fundraising by ensuring compliance with the Association of Fundraising Professionals (AFP) Code of Ethical Standards and Professional Practice.

Community and External Relations

Serve as a champion and ambassador for HSSV, representing the organization at community events, public forums, and key stakeholder engagements.
Build and strengthen strategic partnerships with community leaders, animal welfare organizations, and other nonprofit organizations to expand upon a culture of philanthropy.

QUALIFICATIONS

Proven success and results-driven experience in strategic leadership with multi-channel fundraising programs within a nonprofit organization is a must.
Proven experience leading and developing high-performing teams, with a demonstrated ability to inspire collaboration, drive results, and foster a culture of accountability and excellence.
Proven leadership experience (or capabilities) with cross-functional teams working in a highly collaborative environment.
Ability to develop a multi-year fundraising strategy that includes a strategy that is well supported by analytics and business cases that lead to success.
Deep passion for the mission of HSSV: to save lives, keep families together, and create a better future for pets and their people.
Must excel in key competencies: strategic thinking, integrity and ethical decision-making, strong interpersonal skills, accountability, transparency, and adaptability.
Proven ability to lead change initiatives and cultivate resilient, high-performing teams that adapt to evolving organizational needs.
Exceptional ability to pivot planning between strategy and operations.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrates sound professional judgment, maintains a high level of confidentiality, and applies strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to achieve results.
Outstanding interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust, engage internal and external audiences, and influence outcomes with stakeholders.
Animal welfare experience a plus.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

This position offers a competitive salary range of $230,000 – $250,000, commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage; 403(b) retirement plan; flexible spending accounts; paid time off, and additional wellness benefits.

APPLICATIONS

HSSV has retained the services of Scion, a national executive search firm specializing in nonprofit recruitment, to assist in conducting this important search. For immediate consideration, please apply online with your resume in MS Word format and cover letter.

ABOUT OUR FIRM

Scion is an award-winning retained executive search firm. Through innovative team building and recruitment solutions, Scion seamlessly bridges the gap in interim and executive searches. Our track record and recruitment process have made us one of the top recruitment firms in the nation.

We are proud to be part of the Forbes
lists of the Best Recruitment Firms and the Best Executive Search Firms in America. Additionally, Scion has been recognized as a ClearlyRated
Best of Staffing firm as well as a top recruitment firm by The Business Times
. Additional information about our firm and our practices can be found online.

Scion is an equal opportunity employer and service provider and does not discriminate based on race, religion, gender, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, sexual orientation, disability, political affiliation, or any other protected class. We are committed to the principles of equal opportunity employment and are dedicated to making employment decisions based on merit and value, for ourselves, our client companies, and the candidates we represent.

For opportunities located in a region that has enacted fair chance, arrest, or conviction-based employment ordinances, Scion proactively follows the enacted guidance and considers for employment all qualified applications with arrest and conviction records. We engage in socially conscious business practices and believe that diverse, equitable, inclusive, and non-biased talent and recruitment processes are foundational to the success of Scion as well as every client organization with whom we partner.

jobs.description:
Program Director, Vocational Nursing Program:

Stanbridge University is seeking an experienced, mission-driven Program Director to lead the Vocational Nursing (VN) Program. This role serves as the senior academic and operational leader responsible for program performance, faculty effectiveness, and student outcomes. The Program Director provides strategic direction, ensures academic excellence, and maintains full compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards.

This role is critical to shaping the next generation of licensed vocational nurses through innovative education, student-centered leadership, and dedicated faculty mentorship. Success in this role is measured by program quality, regulatory compliance, and key student outcome metrics, including retention, completion, and licensure pass rates.

Essential Functions:

Oversee the planning, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the Vocational Nursing program
Ensure adherence to regulations established by the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT) and other accrediting agencies
Recruit, supervise, mentor, and evaluate program faculty to ensure effective instruction and alignment with curriculum standards
Lead curriculum design, updates, and assessment processes to maintain relevance and rigor aligned with industry standards and licensing requirements
Monitor and drive student performance metrics (retention, completion, and licensure pass rates) and implement data-driven interventions to improve outcomes
Ensure quality clinical placements in collaboration with clinical partners and the clinical coordination team
Collaborate with university leadership on program budgeting, forecasting, and allocation of instructional resources
Prepare and submit required reports and documentation for BVNPT and accrediting bodies; lead site visit readiness and compliance efforts
Represent the program in professional communities, conferences, and with clinical partners to strengthen relationships and program visibility

Qualifications:

Current, active, and unencumbered Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state of California
Bachelor's degree from a BVNPT-approved school required; Master's degree in nursing, education, or administration preferred
Minimum of four (4) years of experience as a Registered Nurse
At least one (1) year within the last five (5) years in teaching or clinical supervision (or a combination thereof) in a state-approved vocational or registered nursing program; or
A minimum of three (3) years in nursing administration or nursing education within the last five (5) years
Completion of coursework in administration, teaching, and curriculum development from an approved school
Demonstrated leadership ability with strong interpersonal, organizational, and communication skills
Proven commitment to student success, faculty development, and continuous program improvement
Competitive compensation is offered and will be based on education, experience, and internal equity considerations

Conditions of Employment:

A job-related assessment may be required during the interview process
Must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily and be physically present in the office (unless otherwise noted)
Employment Authorization: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Stanbridge University does not provide employment-based immigration sponsorship or participate in employer-sponsored or employer-dependent work authorization programs
Sponsorship: Sponsorship now or in the future could include having Stanbridge University sponsor, complete employer documentation, provide attestations or training plans, or otherwise participate in a work-authorization or employment-based immigration program in order for an individual to begin or continue employment. Stanbridge University does not provide any such sponsorship
Employment verification will be conducted to validate work experience per accreditation standards
Offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check.
Official transcripts are required prior to hire. Degrees earned outside the United States must be evaluated by a recognized credential evaluation service to determine U.S. degree equivalency and applicable subject-area coursework.
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions

Work Environment:

Standard office, classroom, lab, or clinical setting
Duties are typically performed while sitting at a desk or computer workstation
May include time spent in skills labs or bedside environments as required by the program
Subject to frequent interruptions, noise, and demanding timelines

Physical Demands:

Regularly sits for extended periods
Physical ability to perform program- or department-related duties
Proficient in using electronic keyboards and office equipment
Effective verbal communication via phone and in person
Ability to read fine print, operate computers, and understand voices clearly
Able to lift, carry, and/or move objects weighing 10-25 pounds as needed

Employee Benefits:

Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
Retirement Plan (401k)
Exciting university events
Seasonal motivational health and wellness challenges
Work/Life Balance initiatives
Onsite wellness program / Staff Chiropractor
Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)

Diversity and Inclusion: Stanbridge University's motto, "Strength through Diversity," reflects our commitment to fostering an inclusive learning environment and honoring diverse backgrounds
Innovation and Technology: We embrace advanced technology, including simulation and virtual learning, to enhance student outcomes
Community Engagement: Through initiatives such as Stanbridge outREACH, students contribute to local and global communities

jobs.description:
WHO IS CHI?

Community Housing Innovations (CHI) is a not-for-profit housing and human services organization that aims to support social and economic independence. Our vision is to end generational poverty and foster upward mobility by ensuring that all families and individuals live in quality housing, have a home of their own, and a job to support them. CORAZON PURO

Corazón Puro (CP) is an organization dedicated to forming leaders, beginning with Latino youth and young adults, to bring about a Culture of Life. Inspired by the life and Theology of St. John Paul II, these leaders are equipped to become Christ-centered, pure of heart, joy-filled agents of change, in the city and out of the city, in this country and around the world.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Development Director leads Corazón Puro's fundraising strategy and donor relationships, with the goal of building a healthy, diversified funding base to sustain and grow CP's mission. This is a season of transition and growth for CP's development operations; the Director will lead the migration from Pushpay to Bloomerang, strengthen our grants pipeline, deepen relationships with missionary partners, and grow monthly giving. The role requires someone who can build genuine relationships with donors and partners while bringing rigor to systems, reporting, and planning.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Donor Development & Monthly Giving

•      Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with individual and institutional donors and sponsors.
•      Design and lead strategies to grow CP's monthly/recurring donor program as a core, sustainable revenue stream.
•      Establish and maintain warm, consistent communication with individual and business donors.
•     Meet regularly with the Executive Director and senior leadership to align fundraising priorities with organizational needs.
•     Work closely with CP's Founder on the transition and ongoing stewardship of legacy donor relationships, progressively assuming primary relationship management as those relationships are handed off.
Fundraising Events & Campaigns

•     Lead the strategy, revenue goals, and donor-cultivation plan for CP's fundraising events, including sponsorship solicitation and post-event follow-up; event logistics and on-site execution are supported by staff, volunteers, or contracted vendors.
•     Design and lead CP's annual giving campaigns — including the year-end appeal, giving days, and special appeals — setting revenue targets and coordinating messaging across email, print, and social channels.
•     Partner with the program team and graphic designer to produce event and campaign materials, and with the Executive Director to identify event sponsors and host committees.

Donor Systems & Data Transition (Pushpay → Bloomerang)

•      Lead the full migration of donor data and giving history from Pushpay to Bloomerang, ensuring accuracy and continuity of donor records.
•      Establish Bloomerang workflows for gift entry, acknowledgment letters, donor segmentation, and reporting.
•      Train relevant staff and volunteers on Bloomerang and serve as CP's primary point person for the platform going forward.
•      Review data-collection methods across development operations and recommend improvements.
Grant Strategy & Oversight of Outside Grant Consultants

•       Set CP's overall grant strategy: which funders to pursue, how grant revenue fits the broader diversification plan.
•       Serve as CP's primary point of contact and supervisor for any contracted grant-writing agency or consultant, including scoping the engagement, reviewing and approving the contract or SOW, and setting deliverables and deadlines.
•       Review and approve all consultant-drafted proposals, budgets, and reports before submission to ensure they reflect CP's mission and vision, and current program data. 
•       Monitor the consultant's prospect research and grant calendar; hold regular check-ins to track the pipeline of prospective and submitted grants.
•       Evaluate the consultant relationship against agreed KPIs (proposals submitted, win rate, dollars raised relative to fees paid) and bring renewal or termination recommendations to the Executive Director.
Communications & Newsletter

•      Build and maintain a content calendar for donor newsletters and fundraising communications, working cross-functionally with the program team and graphic designer to gather content and produce final materials.
•      Develop print and digital marketing materials that support fundraising efforts, in partnership with the graphic designer.
•      Review fundraising and communications materials and offer recommendations to strengthen messaging.
Missionary Partner Relations

•      Serve as a point of connection between CP and its missionary partners, supporting their fundraising and communication needs.
•      Coordinate with missionary partners on reporting, donor updates, and shared fundraising initiatives.
Reporting & Sustainability

•      Submit regular development reports to the Executive Director and Fiscal Officer.
•      Create post-event reports analyzing results and marketing effectiveness.
•      Assist in creating a sustainable, diversified model for revenue growth, reducing reliance on any single funding source.
•      Assist in the creation of surveys and other metrics to measure program and fundraising effectiveness.
•     Establish a consistent process for gathering data from affiliates and events, ensuring accurate, timely input for the annual report.

QUALIFICATIONS:

•      Committed to living and articulating the teachings of the Catholic Church.
•      Fluent in English and Spanish, written and spoken.
•      Superior writing skills, with experience writing grant proposals and reports, including experience coordinating collaborative, multi-author proposals to deadline.
•      Experience with donor management/CRM systems; experience with Pushpay, Bloomerang, or similar platforms strongly preferred.
•      Demonstrated success building or growing a monthly/recurring giving program.
•      Strong leadership experience and ability to work cohesively across teams.
•      Strong social and interpersonal skills; comfortable representing CP with donors, partners, and Church leaders.
•      Independent worker and thinker who can provide both vision and execution.
•      Ability and willingness to travel as needed.
•      Able to articulate the vision and mission of Corazón Puro and its programs with excellence.

EMPLOYMENT SPECIFICATIONS 

•      This is a full-time, exempt position under the Fair Labor Standards Act.
•     Employee will participate in quarterly performance evaluations with the Executive Director.
•      Performance will be evaluated against development goals set annually with the Executive Director, which may include total revenue raised, growth in monthly/recurring donors, number of grant submissions and award rate, donor retention, and completion of the Bloomerang transition.
•      Employee is subject to a three-month provisional period.  Completion of the provisional period does not change the at-will nature of employment described below, and does not create a contract of employment or any guarantee of continued employment.
•      Employment at Corazón Puro is “at will.” This means either the employee or Corazón Puro may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause, unless otherwise stated.

COMPENSATION

·      Salary range: $100,000, with potential for growth based on experience and demonstrated fundraising results.
·      Health coverage

·      Paid time off
·      Professional development 

The responsibilities above reflect the primary focus of this role. As Corazón Puro grows, additional duties may be added in collaboration with the Executive Director.

To Apply:  

·      Please send your resume to ana@corazonpuro.org with the title Development Director in the subject line.

Reporting directly to the Chief Probation Officer, the 0952 Deputy Director II of Restorative & Prevention Services is a key executive leadership role responsible for directing, strategic planning, and operational scaling across three vital divisions: Pretrial Services, Reentry Services, and Violence Response Services. The Deputy Director provides vision, administrative direction, and executive oversight to ensure seamless, evidence-based, and client-centered care. By leveraging data, expanding service capacity, and cultivating cross-system partnerships with courts, law enforcement, healthcare providers, and community stakeholders, the Deputy Director advances system reform, reduces recidivism, enhances court appearance rates, and promotes long-term public safety and community restoration.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is an accomplished, visionary, and compassionate criminal justice leader with a proven track record of directing complex, multidisciplinary operations and building high-performing teams. This individual possesses deep expertise in evidence-based pretrial practices, risk assessment methodologies, focused deterrence, violence reduction strategies, and continuity-of-care models (including housing stabilization, workforce development, behavioral health, and substance use interventions).

Key professional attributes and competencies of the ideal candidate include:

Strategic & Equity-Centered Leadership: Demonstrated ability to inspire organizational culture, drive care-first reform, address systemic and implicit bias, and elevate professional development for sworn and non-sworn personnel.
Cross-System Collaboration: Expertise in navigating and aligning complex, siloed government systems, collaborating effectively with judges, prosecutors, defense counsel, law enforcement, CBOs, victim advocates, and community leaders.
Data-Driven & Fiscal Acumen: Highly skilled in performance management, outcome evaluation, technology integration, and multi-million-dollar budget oversight, contract administration, and resource allocation.
Subject Matter Mastery: Comprehensive understanding of court processes, criminal records, legal codes, bail statutes, supervision technologies, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive interventions.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

In accordance with Civil Service Commission Rule 109, representative duties include, but are not limited to, the following:

Executive & Strategic Leadership

Provide strategic direction, vision, and administrative oversight for the Pretrial Services, Reentry Services, and Violence Response Services Divisions.
Formulate, enforce, and evaluate division goals, operational standards, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and departmental policies aligned with executive directives and community safety goals.
Serve as a key advisor to the Chief Probation Officer and represent SFAPD in executive decision-making, interagency committees, community forums, and media/public inquiries.
Drive care-first and equity-centered systemic reforms that reduce unnecessary detention, address disproportionate impact, and foster public trust.

Operational Management & Service Integration

Direct division managers and operational teams, ensuring daily service delivery aligns with evidence-based practices, statutory requirements, and quality control standards.
Coordinate and leverage the Community Assessment Services Center (CASC) to establish robust referral pathways for case management, housing, workforce development, legal aid, behavioral health, and court-ordered release conditions.
Oversee the proper application and integration of supervision technologies, electronic monitoring, criminal records systems, and data collection tools.
Review and modernize training curricula for sworn and non-sworn staff to ensure high-quality delivery of trauma-informed, developmentally appropriate, and culturally responsive services.

Fiscal, Contractual & Data Governance

Oversee the development, implementation, and monitoring of multi-million-dollar divisional budgets, resource allocations, and financial reporting.
Manage public and CBO contracts, ensuring optimal resource utilization, operational efficiency, vendor performance, and strict regulatory compliance.
Lead data management, performance metrics, and research efforts to evaluate program impact, inform policy decisions, enhance transparency, and prepare executive reports.

Stakeholder Engagement & Community Partnerships

Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with the Superior Court, District Attorney, Public Defender, Sheriff's Office, law enforcement, CBOs, faith-based partners, and victim advocates.
Conduct stakeholder outreach to secure, maintain, and expand funding, grant opportunities, and strategic support for violence reduction and reentry initiatives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Possession of a Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Criminal Justice, Social Work, Public Administration, Behavioral Sciences, Social Sciences, or a closely related field.
Experience: Three (3) years of extensive management experience leading and directing a complex organization or division providing human, social, or criminal justice services (e.g., pretrial, rehabilitation, social welfare, probation, parole, corrections, law enforcement, or administrative/legal services). All three (3) years must include supervisory experience.
License: Possession of a valid California Class 'C' Driver's License.
Substitution Note: Additional qualifying experience may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis (up to a maximum of 2 years). An advanced degree (Master's or Juris Doctor) in Law, Public Administration, Public Policy, Social Work, or a related field may substitute for one (1) year of the required general experience (supervisory experience remains required).

This position requires the ability to work flexible hours, which may include evening meetings and weekend engagements and work duties as necessary to fulfill departmental and community representation duties.

Desirable Qualifications

Advanced Degree (J.D., M.S.W., M.P.A., M.P.P., or M.S.) in a relevant field.
Demonstrated experience directing multi-divisional operations within a large, complex public or non-profit agency.
Extensive legal background or experience practicing law/providing legal counsel within governmental or criminal justice systems.
Deep knowledge of California legal codes, criminal court procedures, bail statutes, and risk assessment instruments.
Proven expertise in evidence-based practices, including focused deterrence, trauma-informed care, restorative justice, and community-based violence intervention.

Job Function Summary

Involves developing, interpreting and implementing financial concepts for financial planning, resource planning (dollars), and control of organizational budget. May analyze and prepare recommendations for financial plans, including annual resource allocations, future requirements, and operating forecasts.

Generic Scope

Spends the majority of time (50% or more) achieving organizational objectives through the coordinated achievements of subordinate staff. Establishes departmental goals and objectives, functions with autonomy. Manages the accountability and stewardship of human, financial, and often physical resources in compliance with departmental and organizational goals and objectives. Ensures subordinate supervisors and professionals adhere to defined internal controls. Manages systems and procedures to protect departmental assets.

Custom Scope

The Executive Director of Finance together with the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), has primary responsibility for all aspects of the department’s finances. The Executive Director of Finance directs the department’s finance unit and provides the depth and breadth of management, strategic planning, and financial reporting/analysis expertise required in an administratively complex department with an annual operating budget of approximately $75 million, consisting of professional fee activities, professional services agreements (PSAs), extramural awards, sponsored projects, gifts and endowments, state funding, and medical education programs.

The Executive Director of Finance is responsible for developing, planning, and implementing sustainable financial and revenue management to support the department’s strategic initiatives and operations. The Executive Director of Finance develops long-range strategies and solutions for current complex issues that often cross functional areas, while providing the guidance and expertise needed to effectively implement needed changes, using resources efficiently and minimizing risk. The individual is responsible for audit management, internal controls, and risk assessment and abatement. The Executive Director of Finance reports to the Chief Administrative Officer and is a senior member of the department’s leadership team in managing financial issues with a strong emphasis on administrative systems and internal controls. The position works collaboratively with the UCSF School of Medicine Dean’s Office, DPH, FPO, UCSF Health and all internal/external vendors interacting with the department.

Department Overview

The Department of Emergency Medicine (DEM) provides emergency medical care to over 177,000 patients annually at the UCSF Medical Center at Parnassus, UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospitals at Mission Bay and Oakland, and Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital and Trauma Center. DEM administrative and research staff support the work of 90+ full-time faculty and 50+ attending physicians, a residency program, fellowship programs, and over 300 house staff and students each year. Our vision is to be the leader in compassionate, innovative, and equitable emergency care for all people at all times.

Comprehensive knowledge of finance and budget policies, practices and systems; budgeting and reporting techniques; fund accounting; human resource planning; accounting and bookkeeping.
Ability to effectively communicate verbally and in writing in a timely manner.
Interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively across the organization at all levels; ability to interact with diverse populations.
Client services oriented; good listening, critical thinking, and analytical skills.
Ability to multi-task. Strong work ethic, attention to detail, demonstrated success with consistent and timely follow through.
Demonstrated, exceptional planning, problem solving and decision-making skills; demonstrated ability to effectively persuade and negotiate results in complex situations.
At least 6 years of progressively responsible financial management experience, or equivalent experience, encompassing financial management, strategic planning and organizational development, clinical practice management, and human resources management.
At least 5 years of experience as a lead/supervisor/manager.

Knowledge and understanding of internal control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
Familiarity with campus and university systems, federal and staff funding agency requirements, campus internal audit rules and regulations, the campus business and finance bulletin, school and department clinical compensation plan, clinical practice rules and regulations, campus expenditure rules and regulations.
Familiarity with policies and programmatic guidelines for ACGME training programs and associated funding.

Professional certification preferred.

new_jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
new_jobs.description:
Scion Executive Search (Scion)
has been retained to conduct an immediate search for a strategic, collaborative, and mission-aligned Chief Development Officer
on behalf of Humane Society Silicon Valley (HSSV), a highly regarded organization dedicated to animal welfare. This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished fundraising executive to lead impact-driven philanthropy efforts in support of a mission dedicated to saving lives, keeping families together, and creating a better future for pets and their people .
This is a full-time, predominantly onsite role based in Milpitas, California.

ABOUT HSSV

For more than 95 years, Humane Society Silicon Valley (HSSV) has been a leader in animal welfare, serving pets and people throughout the Bay Area and beyond. As an independent, privately funded nonprofit organization, HSSV provides adoption and foster programs, veterinary care, behavior and training support, community programs, regional rescue partnerships, and resources that help pets and the people who love them thrive together.

HSSV is nationally recognized for its leadership and impact in animal welfare, with a long history of developing and sharing approaches that improve outcomes for animals and strengthen the human-animal bond. Through its Animal Community Center, Community Pet Clinic, and a dedicated network of donors, volunteers, partners, and supporters, HSSV works to save lives, keep families together, expand access to care, and build a stronger safety net for pets and people.

Mission, Vision & Values

HSSV is driven by a mission to save lives, keep families together, and create a better future for pets and their people, with a vision of a world where animals thrive, people experience the power of the human-animal bond, and families have the resources and support to care for their pets.

HSSV is grounded in the values of Kindness, Courage, and Impact
which are brought to life through a collaborative culture centered on empathy, gratitude, belonging, continuous improvement, and celebrating shared success. HSSV encourages their teams to think boldly, drive meaningful change, take thoughtful risks, and work across teams to create lasting impact for animals, people, and the communities they serve.

POSITION OVERVIEW

Reporting directly to the President & Executive Director, the Chief Development Officer serves as a key member of HSSV’s executive leadership team, providing strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s high-impact fundraising and donor engagement efforts. This leader will guide the development and execution of long-term philanthropic strategies that generate sustainable revenue, deepen donor relationships, and align philanthropic support with HSSV’s strategic priorities. The Chief Development Officer will play a critical role in advancing HSSV’s mission while fostering a strong organization-wide culture of philanthropy.

The Chief Development Officer will personally cultivate and steward a targeted portfolio of high-value donors and prospects while providing strategic leadership for the Philanthropy team. The role will oversee individual and major giving, annual giving, planned giving, endowment, institutional giving and grants, donor stewardship, partnerships, and major and principal gift prospects. As a senior leader and visible ambassador for HSSV, this individual will also build strong relationships throughout the community to advance the organization’s philanthropic goals.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, results-driven, and highly collaborative fundraising leader who can translate organizational priorities into clear, measurable philanthropic goals. They will foster a culture rooted in transparency, accountability, partnership, and continuous learning while embedding philanthropy as a shared responsibility across the organization. This leader will bring proven success managing multi-channel fundraising programs, developing data-informed multi-year strategies, cultivating high-capacity donors, and inspiring teams to achieve ambitious goals in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Leadership

Lead the strategic direction and execution of HSSV’s multi-year philanthropy strategy, aligning fundraising initiatives, organizational leadership, operational execution, strategic partnerships, and innovative funding opportunities with HSSV’s mission and strategic priorities to drive sustainable revenue growth and maximize philanthropic impact.
Build strong cross-functional partnerships across HSSV, leverage organizational expertise and shared insights to strengthen donor experiences, advance fundraising efforts, and achieve collective goals.
Cultivate, develop, and empower a high-performing team to achieve fundraising goals and ensure long-term success within an inclusive, collaborative, and mission-driven culture.
Direct the development and execution of capital campaigns and other special fundraising initiatives as needed, building the strategy, infrastructure, and leadership necessary to secure philanthropic support for HSSV’s highest-priority needs. This includes partnering with the President & Executive Director, Board, and key stakeholders to develop compelling cases for support, engage lead donors, and drive campaigns to successful completion.
Develop and implement a results-driven framework that establishes clear goals, measures impact, and fosters accountability, excellence, and continuous learning.
Maintain a personal portfolio of major and principal gift prospects and donors, with direct responsibility for achieving an annual individual fundraising goal through the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of high-capacity philanthropists and strategic partners.

Culture of Philanthropy

Develop and oversee a culture of philanthropy that strengthens and grows individual giving, major gifts, annual giving, endowment, planned giving, institutional giving, and grants while building a sustainable pipeline of philanthropic support.
Champion a culture of philanthropy across HSSV by fostering cross-functional collaboration, engaging staff and leadership in fundraising efforts, and embedding philanthropy as a shared organizational responsibility.
Build and steward a robust donor engagement strategy that cultivates lifelong supporters, philanthropic leaders, and community ambassadors who advance HSSV's mission and long-term sustainability.

Program Impact

Drive strategic financial leadership by overseeing budget planning and financial management to maximize fundraising effectiveness and operational efficiency.
Provide strategic oversight of Philanthropy operations to ensure an exceptional donor experience through seamless stewardship, effective talent development, and consistent operational excellence.
Lead the strategic use of data, technology, and analytics to strengthen decision-making, enhance fundraising effectiveness, and drive measurable results.
Model and promote the highest standards of ethical fundraising by ensuring compliance with the Association of Fundraising Professionals (AFP) Code of Ethical Standards and Professional Practice.

Community and External Relations

Serve as a champion and ambassador for HSSV, representing the organization at community events, public forums, and key stakeholder engagements.
Build and strengthen strategic partnerships with community leaders, animal welfare organizations, and other nonprofit organizations to expand upon a culture of philanthropy.

QUALIFICATIONS

Proven success and results-driven experience in strategic leadership with multi-channel fundraising programs within a nonprofit organization is a must.
Proven experience leading and developing high-performing teams, with a demonstrated ability to inspire collaboration, drive results, and foster a culture of accountability and excellence.
Proven leadership experience (or capabilities) with cross-functional teams working in a highly collaborative environment.
Ability to develop a multi-year fundraising strategy that includes a strategy that is well supported by analytics and business cases that lead to success.
Deep passion for the mission of HSSV: to save lives, keep families together, and create a better future for pets and their people.
Must excel in key competencies: strategic thinking, integrity and ethical decision-making, strong interpersonal skills, accountability, transparency, and adaptability.
Proven ability to lead change initiatives and cultivate resilient, high-performing teams that adapt to evolving organizational needs.
Exceptional ability to pivot planning between strategy and operations.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.
Demonstrates sound professional judgment, maintains a high level of confidentiality, and applies strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to achieve results.
Outstanding interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust, engage internal and external audiences, and influence outcomes with stakeholders.
Animal welfare experience a plus.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

This position offers a competitive salary range of $230,000 – $250,000, commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage; 403(b) retirement plan; flexible spending accounts; paid time off, and additional wellness benefits.

APPLICATIONS

HSSV has retained the services of Scion, a national executive search firm specializing in nonprofit recruitment, to assist in conducting this important search. For immediate consideration, please apply online with your resume in MS Word format and cover letter.

ABOUT OUR FIRM

Scion is an award-winning retained executive search firm. Through innovative team building and recruitment solutions, Scion seamlessly bridges the gap in interim and executive searches. Our track record and recruitment process have made us one of the top recruitment firms in the nation.

We are proud to be part of the Forbes

We are committed to the principles of equal opportunity employment and are dedicated to making employment decisions based on merit and value, for ourselves, our client companies, and the candidates we represent.

Ensure adherence to regulations established by the California Board of Vocational Nursing and Psychiatric Technicians (BVNPT) and other accrediting agencies

CORAZON PURO

Corazón Puro (CP) is an organization dedicated to forming leaders, beginning with Latino youth and young adults, to bring about a Culture of Life. Inspired by the life and Theology of St. John Paul II, these leaders are equipped to become Christ-centered, pure of heart, joy-filled agents of change, in the city and out of the city, in this country and around the world.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Development Director leads Corazón Puro's fundraising strategy and donor relationships, with the goal of building a healthy, diversified funding base to sustain and grow CP's mission. This is a season of transition and growth for CP's development operations; the Director will lead the migration from Pushpay to Bloomerang, strengthen our grants pipeline, deepen relationships with missionary partners, and grow monthly giving. The role requires someone who can build genuine relationships with donors and partners while bringing rigor to systems, reporting, and planning.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Donor Development & Monthly Giving

•      Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with individual and institutional donors and sponsors.
•      Design and lead strategies to grow CP's monthly/recurring donor program as a core, sustainable revenue stream.
•      Establish and maintain warm, consistent communication with individual and business donors.
•     Meet regularly with the Executive Director and senior leadership to align fundraising priorities with organizational needs.
•     Work closely with CP's Founder on the transition and ongoing stewardship of legacy donor relationships, progressively assuming primary relationship management as those relationships are handed off.
Fundraising Events & Campaigns

•     Lead the strategy, revenue goals, and donor-cultivation plan for CP's fundraising events, including sponsorship solicitation and post-event follow-up; event logistics and on-site execution are supported by staff, volunteers, or contracted vendors.
•     Design and lead CP's annual giving campaigns — including the year-end appeal, giving days, and special appeals — setting revenue targets and coordinating messaging across email, print, and social channels.
•     Partner with the program team and graphic designer to produce event and campaign materials, and with the Executive Director to identify event sponsors and host committees.

Donor Systems & Data Transition (Pushpay → Bloomerang)

•      Lead the full migration of donor data and giving history from Pushpay to Bloomerang, ensuring accuracy and continuity of donor records.
•      Establish Bloomerang workflows for gift entry, acknowledgment letters, donor segmentation, and reporting.
•      Train relevant staff and volunteers on Bloomerang and serve as CP's primary point person for the platform going forward.
•      Review data-collection methods across development operations and recommend improvements.
Grant Strategy & Oversight of Outside Grant Consultants

•       Set CP's overall grant strategy: which funders to pursue, how grant revenue fits the broader diversification plan.
•       Serve as CP's primary point of contact and supervisor for any contracted grant-writing agency or consultant, including scoping the engagement, reviewing and approving the contract or SOW, and setting deliverables and deadlines.
•       Review and approve all consultant-drafted proposals, budgets, and reports before submission to ensure they reflect CP's mission and vision, and current program data. 
•       Monitor the consultant's prospect research and grant calendar; hold regular check-ins to track the pipeline of prospective and submitted grants.
•       Evaluate the consultant relationship against agreed KPIs (proposals submitted, win rate, dollars raised relative to fees paid) and bring renewal or termination recommendations to the Executive Director.
Communications & Newsletter

•      Build and maintain a content calendar for donor newsletters and fundraising communications, working cross-functionally with the program team and graphic designer to gather content and produce final materials.
•      Develop print and digital marketing materials that support fundraising efforts, in partnership with the graphic designer.
•      Review fundraising and communications materials and offer recommendations to strengthen messaging.
Missionary Partner Relations

•      Serve as a point of connection between CP and its missionary partners, supporting their fundraising and communication needs.
•      Coordinate with missionary partners on reporting, donor updates, and shared fundraising initiatives.
Reporting & Sustainability

•      Submit regular development reports to the Executive Director and Fiscal Officer.
•      Create post-event reports analyzing results and marketing effectiveness.
•      Assist in creating a sustainable, diversified model for revenue growth, reducing reliance on any single funding source.
•      Assist in the creation of surveys and other metrics to measure program and fundraising effectiveness.
•     Establish a consistent process for gathering data from affiliates and events, ensuring accurate, timely input for the annual report.

QUALIFICATIONS:

•      Committed to living and articulating the teachings of the Catholic Church.
•      Fluent in English and Spanish, written and spoken.
•      Superior writing skills, with experience writing grant proposals and reports, including experience coordinating collaborative, multi-author proposals to deadline.
•      Experience with donor management/CRM systems; experience with Pushpay, Bloomerang, or similar platforms strongly preferred.
•      Demonstrated success building or growing a monthly/recurring giving program.
•      Strong leadership experience and ability to work cohesively across teams.
•      Strong social and interpersonal skills; comfortable representing CP with donors, partners, and Church leaders.
•      Independent worker and thinker who can provide both vision and execution.
•      Ability and willingness to travel as needed.
•      Able to articulate the vision and mission of Corazón Puro and its programs with excellence.

EMPLOYMENT SPECIFICATIONS 

•      This is a full-time, exempt position under the Fair Labor Standards Act.
•     Employee will participate in quarterly performance evaluations with the Executive Director.
•      Performance will be evaluated against development goals set annually with the Executive Director, which may include total revenue raised, growth in monthly/recurring donors, number of grant submissions and award rate, donor retention, and completion of the Bloomerang transition.
•      Employee is subject to a three-month provisional period.  Completion of the provisional period does not change the at-will nature of employment described below, and does not create a contract of employment or any guarantee of continued employment.
•      Employment at Corazón Puro is “at will.” This means either the employee or Corazón Puro may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause, unless otherwise stated.

COMPENSATION

·      Salary range: $100,000, with potential for growth based on experience and demonstrated fundraising results.
·      Health coverage

·      Paid time off
·      Professional development 

The responsibilities above reflect the primary focus of this role. As Corazón Puro grows, additional duties may be added in collaboration with the Executive Director.

To Apply:  

·      Please send your resume to ana@corazonpuro.org with the title Development Director in the subject line.
